text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Deputy Health Minister Danute Kuchinskiene was forced to resign on Thursday after she hit a journalist in her office in response to a critical article.
- The prosecutor's office laid charges against the former chairman of bankrupt Tauras Bank and his deputy for misappropriation of funds.
- French President Jacques Chirac said that all the three Baltic countries should start EU entry talks together.
- Estonia's Talinvest bought the whole new share issue of electronic components producer Vingis and now controls 30.3 percent of the firm.
- The issued a state guarantee for a $50 million credit from Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi for the Butinge oil terminal.
- Lithuanian Energy failed to sign an agreement to export electricity to the Kaliningrad region.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told a news conference that his government would do all possible to be in the first wave of EU expansion talks.
- The state's stake in 136 companies, worth a total 61 million litas, will be put up for privatisation in August.
- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta and J.P. Morgan Securities formally signed a contract on a $200 million eurobond.
- China's deputy foreign minister, Zhang Deguang, said during a visit to Lithuania that his country would like to expand economic co-operation between the two states.
- Small and medium-sized businesses account for 68 percent of the GDP.
- The central bank imposed stricter supervision on commercial banks and says their number will decrease.
